meta.titre: Linkage and Crossing Over: from recombinants to crossover values
meta.sous_theme: Linked genes and the crossover value

sections.contenu_markdown: A farmer near Bambili in the North West Region crosses a maize variety with a high yield and a variety that resists disease, hoping to obtain both qualities in the same plants. In some crosses the two traits travel together generation after generation, and in others they are separated much more often than chance alone would suggest. The explanation lies in genes that sit on the same chromosome and in the exchange of chromosome segments during meiosis. GCE Advanced Level papers regularly ask you to write out crosses with genetic symbols, to calculate a crossover value and to explain what that value tells a geneticist.

items: A gene is a length of DNA found at a fixed position, called a locus, on a chromosome, and alleles are alternative forms of a gene.
Homologous chromosomes pair up in prophase I of meiosis and are separated in anaphase I.
In a test cross, an individual of unknown genotype is crossed with an individual that is homozygous recessive for the genes concerned.
Independent assortment of two genes on different chromosomes gives a 1:1:1:1 ratio of phenotypes in a dihybrid test cross.

sections.titre: Linkage, crossing over and the crossover value
sections.contenu_markdown:
**Linkage.** Genes that lie on the same chromosome are said to be **linked**. A chromosome is passed on as one unit, so linked genes tend to be inherited together and do **not** assort independently. A dihybrid test cross involving linked genes therefore does not give the 1:1:1:1 ratio.

**Notation.** Alleles carried on the same chromosome are written together, and the two homologous chromosomes are separated by a line: $\dfrac{AB}{ab}$. In **coupling** the two dominant alleles are on one chromosome ($\dfrac{AB}{ab}$). In **repulsion** each chromosome carries one dominant and one recessive allele ($\dfrac{Ab}{aB}$).

**Crossing over.** In prophase I the homologous chromosomes pair to form **bivalents**. **Non-sister chromatids** of the two homologues may break at the same level and rejoin to each other at points called **chiasmata**, exchanging segments of DNA. The chromatids that result carry new combinations of alleles and are called **recombinant** chromatids. Chromatids that did not exchange material are **parental**. Crossing over does not create new alleles (only mutation does); it shuffles existing alleles into new combinations.

**Gametes from $\dfrac{AB}{ab}$:** parental gametes $AB$ and $ab$ (most frequent), recombinant gametes $Ab$ and $aB$ (less frequent).

**Crossover value (COV).** In a test cross with the homozygous recessive $\dfrac{ab}{ab}$ parent, which gives only $ab$ gametes, the phenotype of each offspring reveals the gamete received from the heterozygote. Therefore:

$$\text{COV}=\dfrac{\text{number of recombinant offspring}}{\text{total number of offspring}}\times 100\%$$

One per cent of recombination is one **map unit** (one centimorgan). If the COV is $x\%$, each of the two recombinant gamete types forms $x/2\%$ of the gametes and each parental type forms $(100-x)/2\%$.

| COV | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0% | Complete linkage, no crossing over between the loci |
| Small (for example 5%) | Genes close together on the chromosome |
| Large but below 50% | Genes further apart, still linked |
| 50% | Behaves as independent assortment (far apart or on different chromosomes) |

variantes.nom: Setting out a linked test cross with genetic symbols
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question says to use genetic symbols to illustrate a cross.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write the lines in this order: (1) phenotypes of the parents; (2) genotypes of the parents, with linked alleles written as $\dfrac{AB}{ab}$; (3) gametes, labelling parental and recombinant types; (4) genotypes and phenotypes of the offspring; (5) the observed or expected ratio. Include a key giving the meaning of each symbol. Parental classes always come out as the larger classes when the genes are linked.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked what a crossover value shows or why it is useful.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A COV is (1) a measure of the relative **distance** between two loci on a chromosome, because the further apart two genes are, the more likely a chiasma forms between them; (2) the basis for building **chromosome maps** that show the linear order of genes; (3) evidence that the genes are linked (a value below 50%); (4) a tool that lets breeders predict how often a desired combination of alleles will appear in the offspring. For loci very far apart, double crossovers cancel each other out, so the COV underestimates the true distance and never exceeds 50%.

variantes.nom: Finding the order of three genes
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the COVs between three pairs of linked genes are given.
variantes.contenu_markdown: The two shorter distances add up to the longest one. If $\text{COV}(X,Y)=a$, $\text{COV}(Y,Z)=b$ and $\text{COV}(X,Z)=a+b$, then $Y$ lies between $X$ and $Z$. The two genes separated by the longest distance lie at the two ends of the map.

sections.enonce_markdown: In a tomato plant, tall stem ($T$) is dominant to dwarf stem ($t$) and round fruit ($R$) is dominant to elongated fruit ($r$). A tall plant with round fruit, true breeding, was crossed with a dwarf plant with elongated fruit. An $F_1$ plant was then test crossed and gave 1000 offspring: 412 tall round, 408 dwarf elongated, 92 tall elongated and 88 dwarf round. Write out the test cross using genetic symbols and calculate the crossover value.

etapes.action: Classify the offspring into parental and recombinant types.
etapes.justification: The dwarf elongated parent produces only $tr$ gametes, so each offspring shows the allele combination of the gamete that came from the $F_1$ plant. The two largest classes are the parental types.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Parental types: tall round (412) and dwarf elongated (408). Recombinant types: tall elongated (92) and dwarf round (88).

etapes.action: Deduce the genotype of the $F_1$ plant.
etapes.justification: The $F_1$ received $TR$ from the tall round parent and $tr$ from the dwarf elongated parent, so the dominant alleles are on one chromosome (coupling). Unlinked genes would give four classes of about 250 each, but the parental classes are much larger, which shows linkage.

etapes.action: Write the test cross with symbols.
etapes.justification: Key: $T$ tall, $t$ dwarf, $R$ round, $r$ elongated. Parental gametes are $TR$ and $tr$, recombinant gametes are $Tr$ and $tR$, and the test parent gives only $tr$.
etapes.resultat_markdown:
Parents: tall round $\dfrac{TR}{tr}$ $\times$ dwarf elongated $\dfrac{tr}{tr}$

Gametes: $TR$, $tr$ (parental); $Tr$, $tR$ (recombinant) $\times$ $tr$

Offspring: $\dfrac{TR}{tr}$ tall round; $\dfrac{tr}{tr}$ dwarf elongated; $\dfrac{Tr}{tr}$ tall elongated; $\dfrac{tR}{tr}$ dwarf round

etapes.justification: COV is the number of recombinant offspring divided by the total number of offspring.
A COV below 50% means that the genes are linked, and it is also the distance in map units.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The loci are about 18 map units apart. Each recombinant gamete type forms about 9% of the gametes ($92$ and $88$ out of 1000), each parental type about 41%.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The genes for height and fruit shape are linked in coupling on the same chromosome; the crossover value is 18%, so they are 18 map units apart.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing the heterozygote as $TtRr$ and predicting a 1:1:1:1 test cross ratio for genes that are on the same chromosome.
items.pourquoi_faux: The ratio 1:1:1:1 is produced only when the two genes assort independently. For linked genes the two parental classes are always more frequent than the two recombinant classes.
items.correction_markdown: Write the heterozygote as $\dfrac{TR}{tr}$ and expect two large parental classes and two small recombinant classes.

items.erreur_markdown: Calculating the crossover value as $\dfrac{180}{820}\times100$, using only the parental offspring as denominator.
items.pourquoi_faux: The denominator of a crossover value is the total number of offspring, parental and recombinant together.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that crossing over takes place between sister chromatids, or during mitosis.
items.pourquoi_faux: Genetic exchange that creates recombinants takes place between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, in prophase I of meiosis.
items.correction_markdown: Say that chiasmata form between non-sister chromatids of a bivalent in prophase I.

items.erreur_markdown: Stating that a test cross gave a crossover value of 60%.
items.pourquoi_faux: A crossover value cannot exceed 50%. At 50% the recombinant and parental gametes are equally frequent, as with independent assortment.
items.correction_markdown: If the recombinants appear to exceed the parental types, the genes are probably unlinked and the value cannot be above 50%.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that crossing over produces new alleles.
items.pourquoi_faux: Crossing over exchanges segments between chromatids and so gives new combinations of existing alleles. New alleles arise only by mutation.
items.correction_markdown: Say that crossing over produces new combinations of alleles (new gametic types).

items.enonce_markdown: In a certain insect, grey body ($G$) is dominant to black body ($g$) and long wings ($L$) are dominant to vestigial wings ($l$). A heterozygous grey long insect was test crossed with a black vestigial insect. The 1000 offspring were: 470 grey long, 455 black vestigial, 40 grey vestigial and 35 black long. Identify the recombinant offspring and calculate the crossover value.
items.solution_markdown:
Parental types are the two largest classes: grey long (470) and black vestigial (455). Recombinant types are grey vestigial (40) and black long (35).

Recombinants $= 40 + 35 = 75$; total $= 1000$.

$\text{COV} = \dfrac{75}{1000} \times 100 =$ **7.5%**.

items.enonce_markdown: In a plant, purple flowers ($P$) are dominant to white flowers ($p$) and long pollen grains ($R$) are dominant to round pollen grains ($r$). A plant of genotype $\dfrac{Pr}{pR}$ (alleles in repulsion) was test crossed with a plant with white flowers and round pollen. The crossover value between the two genes is 16%. (a) Write the genotypes and the percentage of each type of gamete formed by the heterozygous plant. (b) Of 2500 offspring, how many of each phenotype are expected?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Each recombinant gamete type forms $16/2 = 8\%$ and each parental type forms $(100-16)/2 = 42\%$.

Parental gametes: $Pr$ **42%**, $pR$ **42%**. Recombinant gametes: $PR$ **8%**, $pr$ **8%**.

(b) The test parent gives only $pr$ gametes.

| Offspring genotype | Phenotype | Expected number |
|---|---|---|
| $\dfrac{Pr}{pr}$ | purple, round pollen | **1050** |
| $\dfrac{pR}{pr}$ | white, long pollen | **1050** |
| $\dfrac{PR}{pr}$ | purple, long pollen | **200** |
| $\dfrac{pr}{pr}$ | white, round pollen | **200** |

Check: $2 \times 1050 + 2 \times 200 = 2500$.

items.enonce_markdown: Four linked genes $D$, $E$, $F$ and $G$ lie on one chromosome. Test crosses gave these crossover values: $E$ and $D$ 6%; $D$ and $F$ 8%; $E$ and $F$ 14%; $G$ and $F$ 5%; $G$ and $D$ 3%. (a) Deduce the order of the genes on the chromosome. (b) What crossover value is expected between $E$ and $G$? (c) In a test cross producing 3000 offspring for $D$ and $F$, how many recombinants are expected? (d) State two uses of crossover values.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The longest distance is $E$ to $F$ (14). Since $6 + 8 = 14$, $D$ lies between $E$ and $F$. $G$ is 3 from $D$ and 5 from $F$, and $3 + 5 = 8$ is the $D$ to $F$ distance, so $G$ lies between $D$ and $F$.

Order: **$E$, $D$, $G$, $F$** (distances 6, 3 and 5 map units).

(b) $E$ to $G$ $= 6 + 3 =$ **9%**, and $E$ to $F$ $= 9 + 5 = 14$, which is consistent.

(c) $\dfrac{8}{100} \times 3000 =$ **240 recombinants**.

(d) Any two of: constructing chromosome maps; showing that genes are linked; estimating the relative distance between genes; predicting how often a wanted combination of alleles will appear in offspring.

items_markdown: Linked genes are on the same chromosome and are inherited together; a test cross then gives mostly parental types, not 1:1:1:1.
Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes at chiasmata in prophase I and produces recombinant chromatids.
$\text{COV}=\dfrac{\text{recombinants}}{\text{total offspring}}\times100$; 1% is one map unit and the value cannot exceed 50%.
In a test cross, the two larger classes are parental and the two smaller classes are recombinant; each recombinant gamete type is half of the COV.
A crossover value measures the distance between genes, is used to build chromosome maps and to predict the outcome of crosses.
With three genes, the two shorter distances add up to the longest one, and the gene in the middle is the common one.
